question: Which of the following best describes the scope of reproductive health according to standard public health definitions?

options.A: The complete absence of reproductive organ diseases only
options.B: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters relating to the reproductive system
options.C: The biological capability to bear children without medical intervention
options.D: Family planning and contraceptive distribution exclusively

explanation: Reproductive health encompasses physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters relating to the reproductive system, not merely the absence of disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is a major socio-cultural factor negatively impacting reproductive health indicators in Nigeria?

options.A: Universal access to tertiary healthcare facilities
options.B: The complete eradication of harmful traditional practices
options.C: Early child marriage and female genital mutilation
options.D: Equitable distribution of wealth across geopolitical zones

explanation: Practices such as early child marriage and female genital mutilation continue to threaten the health and autonomy of women and girls in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of the National Reproductive Health Policy and Strategic Framework in Nigeria?

options.A: To privatize all maternal and child health services
options.B: To ensure universal access to comprehensive and affordable reproductive health services
options.C: To restrict family planning services to urban areas only
options.D: To eliminate the primary health care system

explanation: The policy aims to improve reproductive health by ensuring universal access to comprehensive, high-quality, and affordable reproductive health services for all Nigerians. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which level of healthcare delivery does the strategic framework heavily emphasize for decentralized interventions?
explanation: The framework emphasizes a primary health care approach to ensure interventions are accessible at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: What was the main purpose of initiatives like the Midwives Service Scheme (MSS) in Nigeria?

options.A: To replace doctors in tertiary hospitals
options.B: To bridge the shortage of skilled birth attendants in rural and underserved communities
options.C: To provide free housing for all healthcare workers
options.D: To promote traditional birth attendance exclusively

explanation: The MSS was established to address the shortage of skilled birth attendants in rural communities to help reduce maternal mortality. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary focus during routine antenatal care visits in Nigeria?

options.A: Providing tetanus toxoid immunizations and malaria prophylaxis
options.B: Scheduling elective cesarean sections for all pregnant women
options.C: Issuing birth certificates prior to delivery

explanation: Antenatal care includes vital interventions such as administering tetanus toxoid immunizations and malaria prophylaxis to protect mother and baby. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: How do family planning and contraceptive services primarily contribute to reducing maternal mortality in Nigeria?

options.A: By completely eliminating the biological need for pregnancy
options.B: By preventing unintended pregnancies and closely spaced births
options.C: By making all childbirths occur exclusively in tertiary hospitals

explanation: Family planning reduces maternal and infant mortality by preventing unintended pregnancies and closely spaced high-risk births. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is an essential responsibility of a nurse or midwife during family planning service delivery?

options.A: Deciding the best contraceptive method for the client without their input
options.B: Providing non-judgmental, client-centered counseling for informed choice
options.C: Refusing service to unmarried adolescents based on cultural norms
options.D: Focusing solely on permanent surgical sterilization methods

explanation: Nurses and midwives must provide non-judgmental, client-centered counseling to help clients make informed choices regarding contraception. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary objective of Adolescent and Youth-Friendly Reproductive Health (AYFRH) programs?

options.A: To restrict healthcare access to married adults only
options.B: To provide safe, judgment-free spaces for young people to access accurate information and services
options.C: To eliminate all educational curricula in secondary schools

explanation: AYFRH programs aim to create welcoming spaces where young people can access accurate reproductive health information and services without stigma. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is community engagement with parents and religious leaders important in youth-friendly programs?

options.A: To secure funding for hospital construction
options.B: To eliminate the need for trained nurses in clinics
options.C: To dispel myths that providing reproductive health education encourages promiscuity
options.D: To enforce mandatory HIV testing for all teenagers

explanation: Community engagement helps sensitize elders and religious leaders, dispelling the myth that reproductive education promotes promiscuity among youths. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT) services in Nigeria?

options.A: To prevent pregnant women from contracting malaria
options.B: To reduce the vertical transmission of HIV from mother to infant using antiretroviral therapy
options.C: To eliminate all forms of sexually transmitted infections in adult males
options.D: To mandate surgical sterilization for HIV-positive mothers

explanation: PMTCT utilizes antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy, labor, and breastfeeding to reduce vertical transmission of HIV to infants. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is confidentiality particularly crucial in the management of STIs and HIV/AIDS?

options.B: Because fear of social stigma and discrimination often deters individuals from seeking care
options.C: Because government policy prohibits recording patient names
options.D: Because lab technicians require anonymity to process blood samples

explanation: Fear of social ostracization and stigma often prevents people from seeking timely medical care, making strict confidentiality essential. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: At which levels of the Nigerian healthcare delivery system do nurses and midwives operate?

options.A: Only at tertiary teaching hospitals in urban centers
options.C: At every tier of the healthcare delivery system from primary to tertiary

explanation: Nurses and midwives operate across all tiers of the healthcare system, from remote primary health centers to tertiary teaching hospitals. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: Besides clinical care and education, what is a key advocacy role performed by nurses and midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: Lobbying policymakers for improved health infrastructure and working conditions
options.C: Replacing government officials in political office
options.D: Enforcing legal penalties for non-compliance with health policies

explanation: Nurses and midwives advocate by lobbying policymakers for better health infrastructure, stable supply chains, and improved working conditions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is a major workforce challenge contributing to poor reproductive health service delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of skilled midwives in rural clinics
options.B: Severe shortages of skilled healthcare personnel driven by migration
options.C: Mandatory retirement at age thirty for nurses
options.D: Excessive funding and resources leading to administrative bloat

explanation: Severe shortages of skilled healthcare personnel driven by internal and external migration pose a major workforce challenge in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h8)

question: Which of the following strategies represents a promising future direction for expanding reproductive health coverage in Nigeria?

options.A: Reducing the number of primary health care facilities
options.C: Leveraging digital health innovations and task-shifting policies

explanation: Leveraging digital health innovations and expanding task-shifting policies are promising approaches to improve coverage and service delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h8)
